# Agent environments

## What an environment is
State, observations, actions, dynamics. The reward is a separate claim about what matters.

## Partial observability (POMDP)
When the agent cannot see the full state it must maintain a belief and sometimes act to gather information. Measurement can be an action with a cost.

## Attention as a hidden variable
Learners do not read everything shown to them. Attention gates learning and drains with fatigue.

# Week 2 build write-up
Built a web-search agent with two tools. Latency was the main issue.

# Evaluating agents

## pass@k vs pass^k
pass@k: any of k runs succeeds. pass^k: all k succeed. Reliability is what deployment needs.

## Proxy vs direct measures
A quiz score is a proxy. Retention a week later is closer to the thing itself.

args.text:
## Evaluation
I evaluated reliability using pass^k, where a build counts as passing only if all k runs succeed rather than just one of them. This is stricter than pass@k and better matches deployment, since a user needs the agent to work consistently across runs. I used at least 3 random seeds and checked whether the writeup/eval workflow completed successfully on every run.

For this build, the main direct measure is whether the agent produces a complete environment definition and an evaluation section with pass^k reported. A quiz score or a single successful demo would only be proxy evidence. In future versions, I would report pass^3 explicitly and include failure cases, since partial observability and hidden attention can make performance vary across runs.

args.text: Totally fair — POMDP just means the agent can’t see the full state. In your case, the hidden part is the student’s attention/understanding: I can see the screen and tool outputs, but I can’t directly observe whether you actually absorbed the reading or are distracted. So I have to infer that hidden state from partial observations like your replies, quiz results, and what’s on screen, then choose actions like explaining, quizzing, or waiting. That’s why this setup is partially observable.
